findings.explanation: getOrganizationFirmwareUpgrades returns top-level upgradeId, upgradeBatchId, network{id,name}, status, time, completedAt, productTypes, toVersion{shortName, firmware, ...} and fromVersion. It has no 'upgrade.' wrapper and no 'productType' field, and the repository's field manifest for meraki:firmwareupgrades agrees.
findings.quote: includes upgrade.toVersion.shortName, upgrade.time, productType for each scheduled or completed upgrade.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the fields as toVersion.shortName, fromVersion.shortName, time, completedAt, status, productTypes and network.name. Note that upgrade records are per network and product type, not per camera serial.

findings.explanation: The add-on's Devices input defaults to a daily interval, but the SPL searches meraki:devices over earliest=-1h. The text never asks the reader to shorten the interval or widen the search window, so most scheduled runs will see no inventory events.
findings.quote: Enable the Devices and Firmware Upgrades inputs in Splunk_TA_cisco_meraki.
findings.suggested_fix: State the Devices input interval (daily by default) and require a search window that covers at least one poll (for example earliest=-25h), or a shorter input interval.

findings.explanation: An exact string comparison flags cameras that are newer than the target (for example on a beta train) as non-compliant. The lookup also needs to use the same string format as the `firmware` field (for example 'camera-4-18').
findings.quote: Trigger a Splunk alert on every camera whose current_fw drifts from recommended_fw.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that target_firmware must use the Devices `firmware` string format, and say how to treat cameras ahead of the target.

findings.explanation: The Meraki add-on is Splunkbase 5580 (Splunk_TA_cisco_meraki). splunkbase.splunk.com/app/5631 returns 404 and is not in the cached catalogue.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the 5631 reference. Retitle the 5580 entry 'Cisco Meraki Add-on for Splunk'.

findings.explanation: A generic Cisco Security support index is irrelevant to MV firmware management.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the Meraki firmware-upgrades API page and Meraki MV firmware release documentation instead.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The append subsearch uses `upgrade.toVersion.shortName`, `upgrade.time`, `productType` and `product`, none of which exist in meraki:firmwareupgrades. The real fields are toVersion.shortName, time and productTypes (see https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/latest/collections/cisco/meraki/organizations_firmware_upgrades_info_module.html and scripts/_meraki_field_manifests.json). The subsearch therefore returns no rows. It also groups by the same field it aggregates, and the appended rows have no serial or model.

`latest(network.name)` on meraki:devices is always null: that sourcetype has only a flat networkId, per scripts/_meraki_field_manifests.json. `earliest=-1h` against a daily Devices input usually returns nothing. Join network names from meraki:organizationsnetworks and widen the window to at least 25h.

summary: The approach (Devices inventory compared against a customer-maintained target-firmware lookup, plus upgrade history) is sound and specific. However, the implementation documents Firmware Upgrades field names that the Meraki API does not return. The SPL's 1-hour window against a daily input and its non-existent network.name field mean it will usually return nothing useful.
